Amina / Atlas security team —

Thanks for the earlier sync. To make our intake efficient for your ISO 27001 + FedRAMP readiness review, we put together an initial control matrix and a scoping diagram (attached). Quick asks:

- Can you confirm the acceptance criteria you need for a submitted control (narrative + evidence checklist)? For example: narrative, config screenshots, log extracts, policy PDF, and evidence extraction window (e.g., 30/90/365 days).
- For SIG/CAIQ items, do you prefer the exported JSON/CSV, a filled spreadsheet, or an annotated PDF?
- Any mandatory artifacts we should prioritize (e.g., KMS attestation, vulnerability scan exports, user access review logs)?
- Preferred file naming / folder structure for Drive intake?

Proposed intake plan: two-week evidence sprint starting Jun 15 — triage owners, collect artifacts, and hand off to you for review. If that works, can we schedule a 30-min intake call early next week to map owners?

Attachments: control-matrix-draft.xlsx, scoping-diagram.png

Thanks — Jordan

From: Amina Hassan <amina.hassan@atlasfin.com>

Subject: Re: Control acceptance criteria and evidence ask for ISO/FedRAMP path

Jordan —

Thanks for the matrix and diagram. High level responses below to help you align artifacts before the intake sprint:

- Acceptance criteria: we require a short control narrative (1–3 paragraphs) outlining the control objective + implementation, plus at least one corroborating artifact. Acceptable artifacts: PDF policy, config screenshot (with timestamps), log extract (CSV or text), or a referenced DocId in our secure Drive. We prefer artifacts that show both config and a recent evidence snapshot (within the sample window).

- Sample windows: for operational controls (e.g., patching, backups, change management) we usually want 90 days; for configuration (e.g., KMS settings) we want current screenshots plus an export showing the last change event. For FedRAMP high/medium baselines, we sometimes ask for 180–365 day samples — we'll flag those where applicable.

- SIG/CAIQ: filled spreadsheet is easiest for reviewers. A JSON/CSV export is fine if you annotate which fields map to our SIG questions. If you provide a single annotated spreadsheet (one row per question with a pointer to the artifact), that will speed triage.

- Must-have artifacts: control narrative, evidence pointer (Drive link or file), KMS attestation (or vendor statement), latest external/internal vulnerability scan results, and privileged access review for admin roles. SOC 2 report is helpful when available but not mandatory at intake.

- Folder structure: one folder per control family, subfolders named by control id (your matrix row id is perfect). Please prefix files with control id_date (e.g., CM-12_20260607_config.png).

We can do the intake call on Jun 10 or Jun 11. Paul (copied) will help with scoping FedRAMP-specific sample windows. I'll follow up with a short intake template (we have an atlas-evidence-template.xlsx) — if you populate it, it will save time.

— Amina
Information Security Manager
Atlas Financial
